v.why: Filling the empty input-to-output edge adds a shallow path and gave large gains on all datasets, whereas replacing an existing op often hurt.
Replacing the residual skip on edge 3 with a conv removes the identity shortcut and caused large drops (-16/-16/-9 and -11/-6/-11).
Adding a residual where there was none yields the largest gains (up to +53 C10), more than swapping a conv for a skip.
Deleting the residual skip in conv-heavy cells is catastrophic (-26 to -34 C100), worse than deleting a conv.
A second skip to the output is redundant when edge 3 already provides a residual path, so the gain vanishes.
With edge 4 empty, removing edge 5 cuts all deep paths to the output and collapses accuracy.
Replacing a useful skip with parameter-free pooling loses both the shortcut and capacity, dropping more than replacing a conv or none.
Swapping a harmful avg_pool for a skip gives larger gains than swapping a conv for a skip.
Replacing the skip on edge 1 with a conv removes a cheap shortcut to node 2 and mostly hurt, unlike replacing none or avg_pool.
In pooling-dominated cells there is little learned depth for a residual to help optimize, so adding a skip gives only small gains.

raw:
Here are 10 hypotheses. Most rest on the edge-3 experiments, which give the cleanest contrasts; the last few rest on only one or two measurements each.

**Edge 3 (the direct input-to-output path) dominates the interactions.**
- **Edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 depends on what it replaces.**
  - Replacing `none` gave gains on all three datasets (experiments 1, 5, 7, 9).
  - Replacing `skip_connect` gave losses in conv-heavy cells (experiments 2, 6).
- **Edge 3 → skip_connect helps most when the edge was empty.**
  - Gains over `none` were up to +53 points (experiments 47, 49, 50, 52).
  - The one swap from a conv gave a smaller gain (experiment 48).
  - In an all-avg_pool cell the gain was small (experiment 51).
- **Edge 3 → none hurts most when it deletes a skip.** Removing a skip in conv-heavy cells cost 25–34 points on C10/C100 (experiments 94, 96).

**Other edges.**
- Adding a skip on edge 4 has little effect when edge 3 already has one (experiment 37).
- Removing edge 5 when edge 4 is already empty collapses the cell (experiment 14).
- `avg_pool_3x3` and `skip_connect` swap symmetrically on edge 4 (experiments 38, 44).
- Replacing a skip on edge 1 with a conv mostly hurts C10 (experiments 88–90).
